claim: Deep brain stimulation targeting the posterior hypothalamus (pHyp-DBS) is being investigated as a treatment for refractory aggressive behavior.
source: Deep brain stimulation targeting the posterior hypothalamus (pHyp-DBS) is being investigated as a treatment for refractory aggressive behavior, but its mechanisms of action remain elusive.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as an established fact about the current state of research.

claim: The mechanisms of action of pHyp-DBS remain elusive.
source: Deep brain stimulation targeting the posterior hypothalamus (pHyp-DBS) is being investigated as a treatment for refractory aggressive behavior, but its mechanisms of action remain elusive.
evidence: This is explicitly stated in the abstract as a knowledge gap.

claim: Ninety-one percent of the patients responded positively to pHyp-DBS treatment.
source: Ninety-one percent of the patients responded positively to treatment, with a more striking improvement recorded in the pediatric population.
evidence: This is supported by data from the 33-patient cohort analyzed in the study.

claim: A more striking improvement was recorded in the pediatric population compared to adults.
source: Ninety-one percent of the patients responded positively to treatment, with a more striking improvement recorded in the pediatric population.
evidence: This is supported by data showing pediatric patients had 93% improvement vs 66% in adults.

claim: Probabilistic mapping revealed an optimized surgical target within the posterior-inferior-lateral region of the posterior hypothalamic area.
source: Probabilistic mapping revealed an optimized surgical target within the posterior-inferior-lateral region of the posterior hypothalamic area.
evidence: This is supported by voxel efficacy mapping analysis of patient data.

claim: Normative connectomic analyses identified fiber tracts and functionally connected brain areas associated with sensorimotor function, emotional regulation, and monoamine production.
source: Normative connectomic analyses identified fiber tracts and functionally connected with brain areas associated with sensorimotor function, emotional regulation, and monoamine production.
evidence: This is supported by structural and functional connectivity analyses using normative datasets.

claim: Functional connectivity between the target, periaqueductal gray and key limbic areas – together with patient age – were highly predictive of treatment outcome.
source: Functional connectivity between the target, periaqueductal gray and key limbic areas – together with patient age – were highly predictive of treatment outcome.
evidence: This is supported by predictive modeling showing R²=0.52 for PAG connectivity and age.

claim: Genes involved in mechanisms of aggressive behavior, neuronal communication, plasticity and neuroinflammation might underlie the functional network.
source: Transcriptomic analysis showed that genes involved in mechanisms of aggressive behavior, neuronal communication, plasticity and neuroinflammation might underlie this functional network.
evidence: This is based on imaging transcriptomics analysis using the Allen Human Brain Atlas.

claim: Aggressive behaviors are highly prevalent among psychiatric patients.
source: Aggressive behaviors are highly prevalent among psychiatric patients, presenting a major obstacle to patient care.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: Aggressive behaviors constitute a leading cause for institutionalization.
source: In addition to suffering, these symptoms constitute a leading cause for institutionalization Gouveia et al., 2021a; Brentani et al., 2013; Gouveia et al., 2019.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Standard treatments for aggressive behaviors involve behavioral and pharmacological therapies that mainly act on the dopaminergic and serotonergic systems.
source: Standard treatments for aggressive behaviors involve behavioral and pharmacological therapies that mainly act on the dopaminergic and serotonergic systems (e.g. serotonin reuptake inhibitors, antipsychotics) Gouveia et al., 2021a; Brentani et al., 2013; Gouveia et al., 2019⁠.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: A substantial proportion (30%) of patients fail to respond to standard treatments and are considered to be treatment refractory.
source: Despite their efficacy, a substantial proportion (30%) of patients fail to respond and are considered to be treatment refractory Adler et al., 2015; Gouveia et al., 2020; Gouveia et al., 2021b.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: DBS is an established therapy for Parkinson's Disease, dystonia, essential tremor, and epilepsy.
source: It is an established therapy for Parkinson's Disease, dystonia, essential tremor, epilepsy Salanova et al., 2021 and obsessive-compulsive disorder Hamani et al., 2014; Li et al., 2020
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: DBS is an established therapy for obsessive-compulsive disorder.
source: It is an established therapy for Parkinson's Disease, dystonia, essential tremor, epilepsy Salanova et al., 2021 and obsessive-compulsive disorder Hamani et al., 2014; Li et al., 2020
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: DBS shows promising results for the treatment of several other neuropsychiatric disorders, including Alzheimer's disease, depression, anorexia nervosa, addiction, and posttraumatic stress disorder.
source: showing promising results for the treatment of several other neuropsychiatric disorders, including Alzheimer's disease Germann et al., 2021a; Lozano et al., 2016, depression, anorexia nervosa, addiction, and posttraumatic stress disorder Elias et al., 2021; Lozano et al., 2008; De Vloo et al., 2021; Elias et al., 2022; Hamani et al., 2022; Davidson et al., 2022.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: To date, DBS for refractory aggressive behavior has primarily targeted the posterior hypothalamic region.
source: To date, DBS for refractory aggressive behavior has primarily targeted the posterior hypothalamic region Gouveia et al., 2019; Gouveia et al., 2021c; Contreras Lopez et al., 2021; Benedetti-Isaac et al., 2015; Torres et al., 2020; Micieli et al., 2017; López Ríos et al., 2023.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The hypothalamus is a diencephalic structure with well-established roles in the control of homeostasis and motivated behaviors.
source: The hypothalamus is a diencephalic structure with well-established roles in the control of homeostasis and motivated behaviors and is a key area in a broader neurocircuitry regulating aggressive behavior that also involves the orbitofrontal cortex, hippocampus, amygdala and periaqueductal gray Dudás, 2013; Blair, 2016; Miczek et al., 2007.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The hypothalamus is a key area in a broader neurocircuitry regulating aggressive behavior that also involves the orbitofrontal cortex, hippocampus, amygdala and periaqueductal gray.
source: The hypothalamus is a diencephalic structure with well-established roles in the control of homeostasis and motivated behaviors and is a key area in a broader neurocircuitry regulating aggressive behavior that also involves the orbitofrontal cortex, hippocampus, amygdala and periaqueductal gray Dudás, 2013; Blair, 2016; Miczek et al., 2007.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Along the anterior-posterior axis, the hypothalamus can be divided into three regions: supraoptic or anterior, tuber cinereum or medial and supramamillary or posterior.
source: Along the anterior-posterior axis, the hypothalamus can be divided into three regions (i.e. supraoptic or anterior, tuber cinereum or medial and supramamillary or posterior) with distinct cell types, projections and functions Dudás, 2013; Beattie et al., 1930.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The anterior region of the hypothalamus is mainly involved in thermoregulation and the control of circadian rhythms.
source: While the anterior region is mainly involved in thermoregulation and the control of circadian rhythms, the medial region regulates feeding and sexual behavior and plays a critical role in several endocrine and autonomic processes Dudás, 2013; Hoff, 1950; Flament-Durand, 1980.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The medial region of the hypothalamus regulates feeding and sexual behavior and plays a critical role in several endocrine and autonomic processes.
source: While the anterior region is mainly involved in thermoregulation and the control of circadian rhythms, the medial region regulates feeding and sexual behavior and plays a critical role in several endocrine and autonomic processes Dudás, 2013; Hoff, 1950; Flament-Durand, 1980.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The posterior hypothalamus (pHyp) is an ergotropic area involved in the generation of sympathetic responses.
source: The posterior hypothalamus (pHyp) is an ergotropic area involved in the generation of sympathetic responses Hess, 1945.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The posterior hypothalamus provides robust projections to the midbrain and reticular formation via the hypothalamotegmental tract.
source: It provides robust projections to the midbrain and reticular formation via the hypothalamotegmental tract, thus being critical in the regulation of wakefulness and stress responses Beattie et al., 1930; Lechan and Toni, 2016; Saper and Lowell, 2014.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The posterior hypothalamus is critical in the regulation of wakefulness and stress responses.
source: It provides robust projections to the midbrain and reticular formation via the hypothalamotegmental tract, thus being critical in the regulation of wakefulness and stress responses Beattie et al., 1930; Lechan and Toni, 2016; Saper and Lowell, 2014.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Lesions located at the pHyp have been reported to cause apathetic and somnolent symptoms.
source: Indeed, lesions (e.g. hamartomas and gliomas) located at the pHyp have been reported to cause apathetic and somnolent symptoms, while the selective neurosurgical ablation of a small portion of the pHyp has been successfully used to treat patients with severe treatment-resistant aggressive behavior (for a detailed review, see Gouveia et al., 2019; Sano et al., 1966; Sano and Mayanagi, 1988).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The selective neurosurgical ablation of a small portion of the pHyp has been successfully used to treat patients with severe treatment-resistant aggressive behavior.
source: Indeed, lesions (e.g. hamartomas and gliomas) located at the pHyp have been reported to cause apathetic and somnolent symptoms, while the selective neurosurgical ablation of a small portion of the pHyp has been successfully used to treat patients with severe treatment-resistant aggressive behavior (for a detailed review, see Gouveia et al., 2019; Sano et al., 1966; Sano and Mayanagi, 1988).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: DBS of the pHyp has been shown to reduce aggressive symptoms in humans, with variable outcomes.
source: More recently, DBS of the pHyp (pHyp-DBS) has also been shown to reduce aggressive symptoms in humans, with variable outcomes Gouveia et al., 2021c; Contreras Lopez et al., 2021; Benedetti-Isaac et al., 2015; Torres et al., 2020; Franzini et al., 2010; Torres et al., 2013; López Ríos et al., 2023.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Only 21 patients diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder, intellectual disability, obsessive-compulsive disorder, epilepsy and schizophrenia with ages ranging from 10 to 51 years have been reported for pHyp-DBS.
source: At present, only 21patients diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder (ASD), intellectual disability, obsessive-compulsive disorder, epilepsy and schizophrenia with ages ranging from 10 to 51 years have been reported, mostly as individual cases or small case series.
evidence: This is stated as a fact about the existing literature at the time of the study.

claim: Long-term improvement in aggressive behaviors following pHyp-DBS was in the order of 38–100% compared to baseline.
source: In these patients, long-term improvement (up to several years of follow-up) in aggressive behaviors was in the order of 38–100% compared to baseline Gouveia et al., 2021c; Contreras Lopez et al., 2021; Benedetti-Isaac et al., 2015; Torres et al., 2020; Micieli et al., 2017; López Ríos et al., 2023.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The study included 33 patients from 5 centers treated with pHyp-DBS to alleviate intractable aggressive behaviors.
source: In this retrospective study, we aggregated a large dataset of 33 patients from 5 centers treated with pHyp-DBS to alleviate intractable aggressive behaviors, characterized by self-injurious and extreme aggressive behaviors towards their surroundings and others (12 females and 21 males, 24.48±10.28 years of age ranging from 10 to 52y, Figure 2A–B).
evidence: This is data from the study cohort.

claim: The cohort included 12 females and 21 males.
source: In this retrospective study, we aggregated a large dataset of 33 patients from 5 centers treated with pHyp-DBS to alleviate intractable aggressive behaviors, characterized by self-injurious and extreme aggressive behaviors towards their surroundings and others (12 females and 21 males, 24.48±10.28 years of age ranging from 10 to 52y, Figure 2A–B).
evidence: This is data from the study cohort.

claim: The mean age of patients was 24.48±10.28 years ranging from 10 to 52 years.
source: In this retrospective study, we aggregated a large dataset of 33 patients from 5 centers treated with pHyp-DBS to alleviate intractable aggressive behaviors, characterized by self-injurious and extreme aggressive behaviors towards their surroundings and others (12 females and 21 males, 24.48±10.28 years of age ranging from 10 to 52y, Figure 2A–B).
evidence: This is data from the study cohort.

claim: The most frequent diagnoses were epilepsy (pediatric: 50%, adult: 62%) and ASD (pediatric: 34%, adult: 24%).
source: The most frequent diagnoses were epilepsy (pediatric: 50%, adult: 62%) and ASD (pediatric: 34%, adult: 24%).
evidence: This is data from the study cohort.

claim: Intellectual disability was observed in all cases.
source: Intellectual disability was observed in all cases.
evidence: This is data from the study cohort.

claim: Intellectual disability was described as severe in 82% of patients and moderate in 18% of patients.
source: This was described as severe in 82% of patients (pediatric: 75%, adult: 85%) and moderate in 18% of patients (pediatric: 25%, adult: 15%).
evidence: This is data from the study cohort.

claim: pHyp-DBS was bilaterally implanted in 30 patients and unilaterally implanted in 3.
source: pHyp-DBS was bilaterally implanted in 30 patients and unilaterally implanted in 3 using either Medtronic Activa (3387 leads in 19 cases and 3389 leads in 10 cases) or Boston Vercise DBS Systems (4 cases).
evidence: This is data from the study cohort.

claim: After treatment, 91% (30 out of 33) of the patients were considered to be responders.
source: After treatment, 91% (30 out of 33) of the patients were considered to be responders (>30% decrease in validated scores compared to baseline) Adler et al., 2015; Gouveia et al., 2020; Gouveia et al., 2021b; Benedetti-Isaac et al., 2015.
evidence: This is data from the study cohort.

claim: The average percentage of improvement was 75.25 ± 29.59%.
source: The average percentage of improvement was 75.25 ± 29.59% (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is data from the study cohort.

claim: Younger patients were found to have a more pronounced benefit, with the pediatric population exhibiting greater symptom improvement compared to the adult population (93% vs 66%).
source: Younger patients were found to have a more pronounced benefit, with the pediatric population (patients ≤ 17 years of age) exhibiting greater symptom improvement compared to the adult population (93% vs 66%, Figure 2D).
evidence: This is data from the study cohort.

claim: No differences were observed between males (75.57% ± 31.13%) and females (74.68% ± 28.00%) in symptom improvement.
source: No differences were observed between males (75.57% ± 31.13%) and females (74.68% ± 28.00%; Figure 2E).
evidence: This is data from the study cohort.

claim: The area of stimulation associated with greater symptom alleviation encompassed 684 voxels associated with a behavioral improvement greater than 90%.
source: This area encompassed 684 voxels associated with a behavioral improvement greater than 90%.
evidence: This is data from the voxel efficacy mapping analysis.

claim: The centroid of the highly efficacious area is located at MNI152 space coordinates x=7.5, y=-15, z=−6.5.
source: The centroid of this highly efficacious area can be found at MNI152 space at the coordinates x=7.5, y=-15, z=−6.5 (https://www.bic.mni.mcgill.ca/ServicesAtlases/ICBM152NLin2009) and in the Talairach-Tournoux space (http://www.talairach.org/) at coordinates x=6.5, y=-16, z=−1.5.
evidence: This is data from the voxel efficacy mapping analysis.

claim: The centroid of the highly efficacious area is located at Talairach-Tournoux space coordinates x=6.5, y=-16, z=−1.5.
source: The centroid of this highly efficacious area can be found at MNI152 space at the coordinates x=7.5, y=-15, z=−6.5 (https://www.bic.mni.mcgill.ca/ServicesAtlases/ICBM152NLin2009) and in the Talairach-Tournoux space (http://www.talairach.org/) at coordinates x=6.5, y=-16, z=−1.5.
evidence: This is data from the voxel efficacy mapping analysis.

claim: The permutation test showed that the voxel efficacy pattern reflects the specific relationship of individual VATs with the individual outcome (ppermute <0.01).
source: The permutation test showed that this pattern indeed reflects the specific relationship of individual VATs with the individual outcome (ppermute <0.01).
evidence: This is data from the statistical analysis of the voxel efficacy mapping.

claim: Structural connectivity analysis identified streamline bundles related to somatosensation (Medial Lemniscus and Spinothalamic Tract).
source: These streamlines bundles may be divided into three main categories of function: I. Somatosensation (Medial Lemniscus and Spinothalamic Tract); II. Regulation of emotions (Amygdalofugal Pathway, Anterior Limb of the Internal Capsule, Medial Forebrain Bundle Nieuwenhuys et al., 2007; Nieuwenhuys et al., 1982); III. Motor Connections (Superior Cerebellar Peduncle, Rubrospinal tract, Frontopontine tract, Central Tegmental Tract, Medial-longitudinal Fasciculus, Motor Projections; Figure 4A–B, Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is data from the structural connectivity analysis.

claim: Structural connectivity analysis identified streamline bundles related to regulation of emotions (Amygdalofugal Pathway, Anterior Limb of the Internal Capsule, Medial Forebrain Bundle).
source: These streamlines bundles may be divided into three main categories of function: I. Somatosensation (Medial Lemniscus and Spinothalamic Tract); II. Regulation of emotions (Amygdalofugal Pathway, Anterior Limb of the Internal Capsule, Medial Forebrain Bundle Nieuwenhuys et al., 2007; Nieuwenhuys et al., 1982); III. Motor Connections (Superior Cerebellar Peduncle, Rubrospinal tract, Frontopontine tract, Central Tegmental Tract, Medial-longitudinal Fasciculus, Motor Projections; Figure 4A–B, Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is data from the structural connectivity analysis with citations supporting the functional categorization.

claim: Structural connectivity analysis identified streamline bundles related to motor connections (Superior Cerebellar Peduncle, Rubrospinal tract, Frontopontine tract, Central Tegmental Tract, Medial-longitudinal Fasciculus, Motor Projections).
source: These streamlines bundles may be divided into three main categories of function: I. Somatosensation (Medial Lemniscus and Spinothalamic Tract); II. Regulation of emotions (Amygdalofugal Pathway, Anterior Limb of the Internal Capsule, Medial Forebrain Bundle Nieuwenhuys et al., 2007; Nieuwenhuys et al., 1982); III. Motor Connections (Superior Cerebellar Peduncle, Rubrospinal tract, Frontopontine tract, Central Tegmental Tract, Medial-longitudinal Fasciculus, Motor Projections; Figure 4A–B, Figure 4—figure supplement 1).

claim: Voxels associated with higher efficacy were more closely related to the identified fiber tracts.
source: Interestingly, when overlapping the voxel efficacy and the structural connectivity maps (Figure 4C), we observed that voxels associated with higher efficacy (in red) were more closely related to these fiber tracts.
evidence: This is an observation from overlaying the voxel efficacy and structural connectivity maps.

claim: Functional connectivity analysis showed that the extent of VAT connectedness to several areas was significantly associated with clinical benefits.
source: The functional connectivity analysis showed that the extent of VAT connectedness to several areas was significantly associated with clinical benefits.
evidence: This is data from the functional connectivity analysis.

claim: Functionally connected areas are related to the production of monoamines (dorsal and medial raphe nuclei [serotonin]; substantia nigra [dopamine]).
source: These areas are related to the production of monoamines (i.e. dorsal and medial raphe nuclei [serotonin]; substantia nigra [dopamine]; Figure 5) and are known to be components of the neurocircuitry of aggressive behavior (e.g. amygdala; nucleus accumbens, rostral anterior cingulate cortex; bed nucleus of the stria terminalis; hypothalamus; dorsal anterior cingulate cortex, insula, periaqueductal grey; Figure 5) Gouveia et al., 2021a; Gouveia et al., 2019; Gouveia et al., 2020; Gouveia et al., 2021b.
evidence: This is data from the functional connectivity analysis with citations supporting the functional roles.

claim: Functionally connected areas are known to be components of the neurocircuitry of aggressive behavior (amygdala; nucleus accumbens, rostral anterior cingulate cortex; bed nucleus of the stria terminalis; hypothalamus; dorsal anterior cingulate cortex, insula, periaqueductal grey).
source: These areas are related to the production of monoamines (i.e. dorsal and medial raphe nuclei [serotonin]; substantia nigra [dopamine]; Figure 5) and are known to be components of the neurocircuitry of aggressive behavior (e.g. amygdala; nucleus accumbens, rostral anterior cingulate cortex; bed nucleus of the stria terminalis; hypothalamus; dorsal anterior cingulate cortex, insula, periaqueductal grey; Figure 5) Gouveia et al., 2021a; Gouveia et al., 2019; Gouveia et al., 2020; Gouveia et al., 2021b.
evidence: This is data from the functional connectivity analysis with citations supporting the functional roles.

claim: The Periaqueductal Grey Matter (PAG) is the only structure that, together with age, significantly predicted more than half of the variance in individual symptom improvement (R=0.72, R2=0.52, p=1.86e-05).
source: The best-performing parsimonious model, which incorporated patient age as well as individual VAT functional connectivity, revealed the Periaqueductal Grey Matter (PAG) to be the only structure that, together with age, significantly predicted more than half of the variance in individual symptom improvement (R=0.72, R2=0.52, p=1.86e-05, Figure 6B, Table 2), retaining significance during leave-one-out cross-validation (LOOCV) (R=0.65, R2=0.42, p=4.406e-5; Figure 6C).
evidence: This is data from the predictive modeling analysis.

claim: The PAG-based predictive model retained significance during leave-one-out cross-validation (LOOCV) (R=0.65, R2=0.42, p=4.406e-5).
source: The best-performing parsimonious model, which incorporated patient age as well as individual VAT functional connectivity, revealed the Periaqueductal Grey Matter (PAG) to be the only structure that, together with age, significantly predicted more than half of the variance in individual symptom improvement (R=0.72, R2=0.52, p=1.86e-05, Figure 6B, Table 2), retaining significance during leave-one-out cross-validation (LOOCV) (R=0.65, R2=0.42, p=4.406e-5; Figure 6C).
evidence: This is data from the cross-validation analysis.

claim: Connectivity with PAG and limbic structures (amygdala, anterior cingulate cortex, bed nucleus of the stria terminalis, left nucleus accumbens, right orbitofrontal cortex, right fusiform gyrus) was superior in predicting outcome.
source: Indeed, connectivity with PAG and limbic structures, namely the amygdala (R=0.75, R2=0.57, p=4.20e-07), anterior cingulate cortex (rostral: R=0.76, R2=0.58, p=2.75e-07; dorsal: R=0.75, R2=0.57, p=3.96e-07), bed nucleus of the stria terminallis (R=0.76, R2=0.58, p=2.75e07), left nucleus accumbens (R=0.76, R2=0.58, p=8.51e-07), right orbitofrontal cortex (R=0.76, R2=0.58, p=2.75e-07) and right fusiform gyrus (R=0.75, R2=0.56, p=4.67e-07) was superior in predicting outcome.
evidence: This is data from the predictive modeling analysis.

claim: Gene set analysis identified genes associated with brain structures at the core of the neurocircuitry of aggressive behavior (Hypothalamus, Amygdala, Prefrontal Cortex and Cingulate Cortex).
source: We observed genes associated with clinically relevant brain areas considered to be at the core of the neurocircuitry of aggressive behavior (i.e. Hypothalamus, Amygdala, Prefrontal Cortex and Cingulate Cortex) Gouveia et al., 2021a; Gouveia et al., 2019; Gouveia et al., 2020; Gouveia et al., 2021b; Blair, 2016
evidence: This is data from the imaging transcriptomics analysis with citations supporting the functional relevance.

claim: Gene set analysis identified genes linked to oxytocin, a peptide hormone critically implicated in social behaviors.
source: genes linked to oxytocin (a peptide hormone critically implicated in social behaviors) Ne'eman et al., 2016; Johansson et al., 2012; Neumann, 2008; Malik et al., 2012; Amorim et al., 2018
evidence: This is data from the imaging transcriptomics analysis with citations supporting the functional relevance.

claim: Gene set analysis identified genes related to cell compartments involved in neuronal communication and plasticity (neuron projection, synapse; axon guidance, long-term potentiation).
source: and to cell compartments related to neuronal communication and plasticity (e.g. neuron projection, synapse; axon guidance, long-term potentiation).
evidence: This is data from the imaging transcriptomics analysis.

claim: There was a significant overrepresentation of genes associated with oligodendrocytes compared to the expected distribution of genes per cell type.
source: Additionally, investigating the prevalence of cell types associated with the set of genes identified in our analysis, we found a significant overrepresentation of genes associated with oligodendrocytes and an underrepresentation of genes associated with astrocytes and microglia when compared to the expected distribution of genes per cell type (Figure 7).

claim: There was an underrepresentation of genes associated with astrocytes and microglia compared to the expected distribution of genes per cell type.

claim: The response rate for pHyp-DBS was high, with 91% (30 out of 33) of patients qualifying as treatment responders.

source: and the average improvement across the whole pHyp-DBS cohort was 75%.

source: These results are in line with previous work showing that symptom improvement following hypothalamic neurosurgery for the treatment of aggressive behavior is in the order of 90% Gouveia et al., 2019.
evidence: This is a comparison with previous literature supported by citation.

claim: Outcomes in patients implanted with directional DBS electrodes or conventional electrodes were found to be comparable.
source: In our series, four patients were implanted with directional DBS electrodes. Outcomes in patients implanted with these systems or conventional electrodes were found to be comparable Contreras Lopez et al., 2021.

claim: The brain only fully achieves maturity in early adulthood.
source: Considering that the brain only fully achieves maturity in early adulthood Gallagher et al., 2019

claim: DBS is primarily used for the treatment of neurological and psychiatric disorders in adults.
source: DBS is primarily used for the treatment of neurological and psychiatric disorders in adults and is emerging as an effective and safe therapy for neurological diseases in children Lipsman et al., 2010

claim: One of the most commonly targeted areas in hypothalamic neurosurgery lies along the midpoint of the line between the anterior and posterior commissures (AC-PC line), in a region anterior to the rostral end of the aqueduct, posterior to the anterior border of the mammillary body and superior to the red nucleus.
source: One of the most commonly targeted areas in those series lies along the midpoint of the line between the anterior and posterior commissures (AC-PC line), in a region anterior to the rostral end of the aqueduct, posterior to the anterior border of the mammillary body and superior to the red nucleus Sano and Mayanagi, 1988

claim: Normative connectivity analyses rely on high-quality atlases derived from very large cohorts of healthy subjects (around 1000 brain scans).
source: Unlike patient-specific studies, where functional MRI and diffusion-weighted images are acquired from a single patient, normative analyses rely on high-quality atlases derived from very large cohorts of healthy subjects (around 1000 brain scans).

claim: Normative connectivity data have been previously shown to generate results that are comparable to patient-specific imaging data.
source: Although normative connectivity data may not fully capture patient- or pathology-specific variations, they have been previously shown to generate results that are comparable to patient-specific imaging data Elias, 2022; Wang et al., 2021.

claim: Patients with neurodevelopmental disorders, especially those presenting with self-injurious behavior, are known to frequently have altered sensory perception (including reduced pain sensitivity).
source: Indeed, patients with neurodevelopmental disorders, especially those presenting with self-injurious behavior, are known to frequently have altered sensory perception (including reduced pain sensitivity), which can contribute to the chronicity and severity of the behaviour Gouveia et al., 2021a; Koenig et al., 2017.
